titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spells 29, 27, 58 and 59
part: Spells 29, 27, 58 and 59 — keeping the heart; breath and water in the necropolis (Plates 15–16)
work: Book of the Dead of Ani
workEn: Book of the Dead of Ani
draftNote: Draft — the hieroglyphs are read from the printed type of Budge's 1895 edition of the papyrus, and the signs and readings are still being checked; expect changes.
source: Papyrus of Ani (British Museum EA 10470), Plates XV, XVI. Hieroglyphs transcribed from the interlinear text of E. A. W. Budge, The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum (London, 1895), pp. 96–105; Budge's transliteration and word-by-word English were used to check the reading of the signs and the sense, never for wording. Only the papyrus's own text is given: the passages Budge supplies from other papyri in his appendixes and footnotes are left out. Transliteration in the Leiden convention, with the reed written i; translation made fresh from the Egyptian. Shown left to right; the papyrus is written in columns read from the top down. The line under each word ("say") is the conventional Egyptological classroom pronunciation — a neutral e between consonants; ꜣ and ꜥ as a; w as u or w; ṯ as tj; ḏ as dj; ḫ and ẖ as kh; š as sh — an artificial teaching pronunciation, since the vowels of Egyptian were never written. The grouping of signs within a word follows Budge's type, which regularises the scribe's hand.
about: Four short spells on Plates 15 and 16 of Ani's papyrus, written after Spells 61 and 54. In Spells 29 and 27 Ani keeps his heart: he turns back a messenger of the gods who has come for it, and he tells the takers of hearts that his heart is his own and obeys him. In Spells 58 and 59 he asks for breath and water in the necropolis: he answers the keepers of a door, names the parts of his boat, and begs water and air from the sycamore of the sky-goddess Nut. Budge prints three chapters from other papyri between Spells 27 and 58, which are left out; many words here are rare or doubtful, and the notes say so.

sentences.i: Spell for not letting the heart of a man be taken away from him in the necropolis.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḥm·tw; read nḥm·tw. The bowl ḥm (coded N41, approximate) with m as complement, t and the chick w are printed, but not the water n with which nḥm 'take away' begins; the same title in Spell 61 has it, and the sense allows no other word. Spell 29 begins. The papyrus writes rꜣ n tmt rdit ḥm·tw in red, then ib n s in black, m-ꜥ·f in red again, and m ẖrt-nṯr in black. ·tw makes the passive sḏm·tw·f after rdi, 'letting (the heart) be taken away'. rꜣ n 'spell for' is the mouth with its stroke and water n, as in every title. tmt is t, the sledge tm (U15) and the owl m as complement, with a second t after them: the negative verb tm 'not to do', as in Spell 61, where the second t is not written (Budge also reads temt). rdit is the mouth r, t and the arm (D36, no loaf): the negatival complement, 'not letting'. ib 'heart' is the heart with its stroke, and ib n s 'the heart of a man' is the genitive written with n; s is the bolt, a stroke and the seated man. m-ꜥ·f 'from him' is the compound preposition m-ꜥ, here the owl m with the arm ꜥ drawn across it in one ligature, and the viper ·f. m 'in' is the sign m (Aa15), and ẖrt-nṯr 'the necropolis' is the flag nṯr, written first out of respect, the loop r (coded D21, approximate) and the block ẖr (T28), as in Spell 61. The heart (ib) was the seat of mind and memory: without it the dead man could neither think nor answer at the judgement.

sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani, true of voice: Back, you messenger of every god!
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red. ḏd in N 'said by N', as before: the cobra and the hand in one ligature, then in, written here with the sign in (coded W25, approximate) and water n as complement. wsir is the low seat (coded Q2, approximate) over the eye, ꜣny has the squatting man with a flail (A52), and mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice' is the plinth mꜣꜥ and the oar ḫrw, without the sickle. ḥꜣ·k is the papyrus clump ḥꜣ (M16) with ꜣ as complement, a small head (coded D1, approximate) as classifier, and ·k: the preposition ḥꜣ 'behind' with a suffix, 'behind you!', the cry that turns something back, as in Spell 17. wpwty 'messenger' is the horns wp (coded F13, approximate) with p as complement, t, the chick w and two strokes y; the t is written before the w (Budge: àptui). Budge prints a small × high above the walking legs at the end; it is taken as the crossed sticks (Z9), the classifier of crossing that wpwtyw has in the Address of Spell 125, and the legs as the classifier of going. The × may instead be a printer's mark. n nṯr nb 'of every god': water n, the flag with the seated god, and the basket nb, 'every' after its noun. The messengers of the gods were sent to fetch and to punish; this one has come for Ani's heart.

sentences.i: Have you come for this heart of mine, which belongs to the living?
sentences.n: in, the reed and water n, and iw, the reed and the chick, open the sentence together: in iw marks a question, 'is it that …?' (Budge: àn àu, 'is it that'). Neither is translated on its own. ii·n·k 'you have come' is the reed with legs (M18), which writes ii 'come', the reed i as complement, the walking legs (printed as a small Λ), water n and the basket ·k: the sḏm·n·f. r 'for' is the mouth. ḥꜣty·i 'my heart' is the forepart of a lion ḥꜣt with t as complement, two strokes y, the heart as classifier and the seated man ·i, as in Spell 26; the second word for heart, beside ib. pn 'this' (p and n) follows the suffix, as it must. n ꜥnḫw is the genitive n with ꜥnḫw 'the living', the sign ꜥnḫ (S34) with n and ḫ as complements, the chick w and a stroke. Budge takes it as 'which liveth'; the genitive with the plural noun gives 'of the living', a heart that belongs among the living. The next line writes the same word with the seated man, the classifier of people, which supports that reading. Ani speaks to the messenger.

sentences.i: This heart of mine, which belongs to the living, shall not be given to you.
sentences.n: nn is the negative arms (coded D35, approximate) with water n: with the sḏm·f, 'shall not', the negative of the future. Budge prints ṭātu-nek as one group; it is split here into di·tw and n·k (q re-indexed). di·tw is the giving hand with its loaf (D37), the form of rdi without its r, then t and the chick w: the passive sḏm·tw·f, '(shall not) be given'. n·k 'to you' is water n and ·k. ḥꜣty·i pn n ꜥnḫw as in the line before; here ꜥnḫw has the seated man and a stroke as classifiers, the sign of people. The question was a challenge, and this is the refusal: the heart stays with its owner.

sentences.i: Striding(?), the gods hear the offerings made to me, and they fall on their faces, all of them(?), to the ground of their own accord.
sentences.n: The passage is obscure, and the rendering follows the order of the signs. ḫndw is ḫ and water n, then the mountain (coded N26, approximate), which writes ḏw, standing here for d, then the chick w and the walking legs (a small Λ): taken as ḫnd 'tread, stride', the w being the plural ending of a participle, not a complement of the mountain (Budge: χenṭu, 'advancing'). Who strides is not said. sḏm 'hear' is the ear (F21) with m as complement, and nṯrw 'the gods', the flag three times, is its noun subject: the sḏm·f, 'the gods hear'. ḥtpt 'offerings' is the offering-mat ḥtp (R4) with t and p as complements and t. Budge prints the mouth r and the seated man as two groups and marks the r (sic); they are joined here as r·i 'to me' (q re-indexed). If the r is a slip, the phrase is ḥtpt·i 'my offerings'; the reading keeps what stands. ḥr, the face with its stroke, has no English in Budge. It is taken as the preposition ḥr with the infinitive ḫr 'fall', whose subject is the suffix: 'and they fall', what follows on the hearing. ḫr·sn is ḫ and r with a falling man (coded A15, approximate) as classifier, and ·sn (the bolt, water n and plural strokes). ḥr ḥr·sn 'on their faces': the preposition, then the noun 'face' with ·sn, both the face with its stroke. The next group is the bolt, t and water n, then the owl m, and t over plural strokes; Budge marks it (sic) twice and reads temt, 'all of them'. The bolt and the water n are not explained. It is taken with him as tmt 'all', from tm 'be complete', but the reading is doubtful. m tꜣ 'to the ground' is the owl and the strip of land with grains (coded N16, approximate). ḏs·sn is the cobra ḏ and the bolt s with plural strokes, and ·sn: ḏs 'self', 'of their own accord'. The gods bow to the ground before one who receives offerings: the speaker claims the rank of a god. Spell 29 ends here.

sentences.i: Spell for not letting the heart of a man be taken from him in the necropolis.
sentences.n: Spell 27 begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes rꜣ n tmt rdit iṯ in red, ḥꜣty n s in black, m-ꜥ·f in red, and m ẖrt-nṯr in black. rꜣ n tmt rdit as in Spell 29. iṯ 'take' is the tether ṯ with the walking legs under it, the one sign that writes iṯ (V15; coded here as the tether V13, approximate, and the legs), then t, written for ṯ as a complement, and the low hooked sign (U15), the sign printed for the arm with a stick, the classifier of force (Budge: θet). No reed i and no tw are written. It is taken as the passive sḏm·f after rdi, 'letting (the heart) be taken', as the nḥm·tw of Spell 29 asks; 'letting (anyone) take' is also possible. ḥꜣty 'heart' is the forepart of a lion ḥꜣt with t, two strokes y and the heart as classifier: the second word for heart. s, m-ꜥ·f, m (the owl here) and ẖrt-nṯr as in Spell 29. The two heart spells stand side by side on the papyrus, one after the other.

sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red; the name is black. ḏd in wsir ꜣny as in Spell 29: Budge prints no transliteration under the cobra and hand, but they are the same ligature. ꜣny has the squatting man with a flail. i 'O' is the reed with the man with hand to mouth (A2), the gesture of calling. iṯyw is iṯ 'take', written as in the title, with two reeds y and a stroke: the plural participle, 'those who take', its w not written (Budge: θeti, 'takers away'). ibw 'hearts' is the heart with two strokes, the second tall and dashed, for the plural, and iṯyw ibw is the direct genitive, 'takers of hearts'. The next word, which Budge prints at the head of Plate 16, is water n, the hill-slope q (N29), the viper f, two reeds y, the chick w, t, the low hooked sign (U15) and a stroke. It is not known. Budge reads neqefiut and renders '[hail] stealers [of hearts]', supplying the bracketed words. The low sign may be the classifier of force, which would suit a verb of seizing or striking, but that is a guess, and the word is left untranslated. The takers of hearts are demons who rob the dead of the heart, and with it of mind and memory.

sentences.n: The papyrus writes sḏm with the plinth mꜣꜥ (Aa11) as its complement; read sḏm·k, with the sign m (Aa15). sentences.i: The Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice in peace, true of voice in the beautiful West, on the place(?) of eternity.
sentences.n: wsir is the eye, the seat (Q1) and the seated god, and sš 'scribe' is the palette (Budge: ān); ꜣny has the squatting man with a flail. m ḥtp 'in peace' is the sign m (Aa15) and the offering mat ḥtp with t. The second mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written out: the sickle mꜣ, the arm ꜥ, the oar ḫrw, the chick w and the man with hand to mouth. imntt 'the West' is the emblem of the West with t twice and the hill-country sign. nfrt 'beautiful' is the heart and windpipe nfr with f, t and r, the t printed before the r: feminine to agree with imntt. ḥr 'on' is the face. The next word is the bolt s (coded O34, approximate) and t with the hill-country sign (N25); Budge reads set, 'the mountain'. It is taken as st 'place', with the classifier of the desert hills where the dead were buried; with an m that is not written, it could be smyt 'desert, necropolis'. nt is the feminine genitive, and ḥḥ is nḥḥ 'eternity', written as in line 2. The spell closes with Ani's name and titles. After this unit Budge prints Spells 29A, 30A and 28 from Naville's edition: other papyri have these spells here, and Ani's papyrus goes on with Spell 58.

sentences.i: Spell for breathing air and having power over water in the necropolis.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes sst; read ssn. The word is the folded cloth s twice, a small nose (coded D19, approximate) as classifier and t, where Spell 54 has water n; the nose and the air allow no word but ssn 'breathe' (Budge: seset). Spell 58 begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes rꜣ n ssn nfw sḫm m mw m in red, and ẖrt-nṯr in black. The same writing comes back three times in Spell 59, and the reading is corrected there in the same way. nfw 'air' is the sail (coded P5, approximate) with the chick w and a stroke, as in Spell 54. sḫm 'having power' is the sceptre sḫm with m and the low hooked sign (U15), the classifier of force: an infinitive like ssn, joined to it without 'and'. m mw 'over water': the owl and three lines of water. m ẖrt-nṯr as in Spell 29. Breath and water are what the dead most need, and the spell asks for both.

sentences.i: May you give me a jug of milk, a cake, a loaf(?), a portion(?) and plenty of meat in the mansion of Anubis.
sentences.n: Budge prints erṭāi-ten-nà as one group; it is split here into rdy·tn and n·i (q re-indexed). rdy·tn is the mouth r, the arm (D36, no loaf), two reeds y and ·tn: rdi 'give', its weak y written, in the sḏm·f used as a wish, 'may you give'. The 'you' is plural, the gods of the mansion. mhr 'jug' is the owl with the arm, read m as in mḫnt, the courtyard h, r, the reed and a small lidded pot with lugs (coded W22, approximate) as classifier (Budge: māḥerà); the reed is not explained. n irtt 'of milk': irtt is the reed, the eye ir, t twice and two milk-jugs in a net (coded W20, approximate) with a stroke. šns 'cake' is the cord šn (V7, approximate) with n, the bolt s and a long loaf (coded X4, approximate), as in the rubric of Spell 125. The next word is the house (O1), the bolt s, two strokes and a loaf (X4, approximate). Budge reads pasi, 'loaves', as if the first sign were the stool p; in the type it is the house, which writes pr. It is taken, by its loaf, as a kind of bread, psy, not known otherwise; the reading is doubtful. dni is the hand d, water n and two strokes y with the lugged pot: dni 'portion, share', here a measure of drink by its pot (Budge prints ṭeni (sic), 'cups of drink'). wr n iwf 'plenty of meat': wr, the swallow with r, used as a noun, 'a great amount', the genitive n, and iwf 'meat', the reed, the chick w and f, with a piece of flesh (coded F51, approximate) and plural strokes. Budge's numeral 7 is printed inside iwf, before the flesh, and his line 7 begins with the m after it. m ḥwt nt inpw 'in the mansion of Anubis': ḥwt as in line 3, and inpw 'Anubis', the reed, n, p and w, with the jackal-headed god (C6). Anubis, the god of embalming, watched over the offerings at the tomb.

sentences.i: If this spell is known, he will go in after coming forth from the necropolis.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir rḫ rꜣ pn iw·f ꜥq·f m-ḫt prt m in red; ẖrt-nṯr and the last word are black. This is the rubric of Spell 58, the note on its use that follows the spell. ir 'if' is the reed and r. rḫ 'is known' is r and ḫ with the roll: the passive sḏm·f, without an ending. rꜣ pn 'this spell'. iw·f ꜥq·f 'he will go in' is iw with ·f, then the cormorant ꜥq (coded G35, approximate) with q and the walking legs, and ·f: iw·f sḏm·f, a statement of what will happen. m-ḫt 'after' is the owl and the branch ḫt (M3) with ḫ and t as complements and the walking legs: the compound preposition. prt 'coming forth' is the house pr with r, the walking legs and t: the infinitive of pri. m ẖrt-nṯr is written out here: the flag, the block ẖr over r, t and the hill-country sign (coded N25, approximate). A last nt, water n and t, has no English in Budge; it is not translated, and it may begin a phrase that was not finished. To go out and come back in again is the freedom of the dead, and the rubric promises it.

sentences.i: May you give me some of the water and air that are in you.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes n; read mw. Only one line of water is printed, and Budge queries his mu; the titles have mw 'water', and the sense needs it. Budge prints ṭāt-nà as one group; it is split here into di·t and n·i (q re-indexed). di·t is the giving hand with its loaf (D37) and t, the suffix ·t 'you', feminine, for the sycamore: rdi without its r, in the sḏm·f used as a wish, 'may you give'. m is the owl: m of a part, 'some of'. Budge's numeral 2 stands before nfw 'air', and no word for 'and' is written. im·t 'in you' is the reed, the owl and the crossed planks im (Z11): im written out before its sign, the form of m before a suffix, with t, the feminine suffix (Budge: àmt). The tree of the sky-goddess is asked to share what it holds.

Budge prints two groups, neḳeḳ and ur, and they are joined here as one name, as in Spell 54 (q re-indexed); here the goose is the classifier of ngg, and wr has its own bird. The Great Cackler is the goose of the beginning of things, whose egg held the first life.

glossary.n: n — not; negates the verb ('I have not …') · also in n wn "there is not" · a second word of the same spelling: the preposition "to, for" (n·i "to me") · the negative also before a noun, 'without, there being no …' · the preposition also 'because of, on account of'
glossary.ḫnd: ḫnd — to tread, step, walk (on) (verb; ḫnd ḥr 'tread upon') · a second word of the same spelling: leg, shin (noun; reading uncertain)
glossary.ḥr: ḥr — face; (preposition) upon, on, over, concerning · a second word of the same spelling: Horus, the falcon god, son of Osiris and Isis; the sun as a falcon (god's name; Budge: Ḥeru) · also 'at' (ḥr sbꜣw 'at the gates'); ḥr-tp 'upon' (compound preposition: ḥr + tp 'head') · also for, on behalf of; on account of (preposition; ḥr·k 'for you') · also 'with' (of the cause of a feeling: ḥtp ḥr·s 'content with it')
glossary.ḫr: ḫr — to fall (verb) · a second word of the same spelling: to, near, with (preposition; of persons) · also 'before' (ḫr nṯrw 'before the gods') · a third word: the particle ḫr, which brings in a further case or a consequence (?) (particle; sometimes written ẖr) · also 'from' (of persons: ḫr s nty·f ḫr·f 'from the man with whom it is')
glossary.·sn: ·sn — they, them, their (3rd person plural suffix pronoun)
glossary.tꜣ: tꜣ — to be hot; tꜣ-ib 'hot-tempered' · a second word of the same spelling: land, earth (noun; plural tꜣw 'lands'; dual tꜣwy 'the Two Lands', Egypt; tp tꜣ 'upon earth')
glossary.ḏs: ḏs — self (noun; with a suffix, ḏs·f 'himself, by himself, of his own accord')
glossary.iṯi: iṯi — to take, seize, take possession of (verb 3ae-inf; participle iṯ 'who took')
glossary.i: i — O!, hail (the vocative interjection that opens each declaration)
glossary.nqfywt: nqfywt — a word not known; perhaps of seizing or striking, from its classifier of force (?) (Budge: neqefiut, 'stealers')
glossary.ir: ir — to do, make (lemma iri) · a second word of the same spelling: the particle ir "when, if" at the head of a clause (ir ꜥq·i "when I entered"), here apparently also bringing in a question ("do you know …?") · also "as for" (particle; ir with a noun puts that noun first as the topic)
glossary.·tn: ·tn — you, your (2nd person plural suffix pronoun)
glossary.ind: ind — hail! greetings! (interjection; from i 'O' and nḏ 'greet'; ind ḥr·k 'hail to you', literally 'greetings to your face')
glossary.nḥḥ: nḥḥ — eternity, endless recurrence of time (noun m.; paired with ḏt)
glossary.ẖry: ẖry — lower, who/which is beneath (nisba of ẖr) · also, perhaps, who holds, has in keeping (?) (plural ẖryw; Budge: χeri, 'possessors of')
glossary.ḏt: ḏt — everlastingness, time as unchanging permanence (noun f.; paired with nḥḥ) · a second word of the same spelling: body, person (noun f.)
glossary.im: im — there, therein (adverb; nty im "he who is there")
glossary.sḫpr: sḫpr — to bring into being, create; to bring about (verb; causative of ḫpr)
glossary.ḏw: ḏw — evil, bad; an evil deed (adjective, noun; written with the mountain ḏw)
glossary.ḥr-ntt: ḥr-ntt — because (conjunction: ḥr 'on account of' + ntt 'that')
glossary.iry: iry — one who belongs to, keeper of (nisba of r "to"; iry ꜥꜣ "doorkeeper") · also as an adjective, 'belonging to, pertaining to' (feminine irt; irt·f 'which belongs to him')
glossary.ꜥꜣ: ꜥꜣ — great (adjective); (adverb) here, hither · a second word of the same spelling: donkey, ass (noun) · a third word of the same spelling: door, door-leaf (noun; iry-ꜥꜣ "doorkeeper") · also greatly, very (adverb, after an adjective or participle: ḥsy ꜥꜣ 'greatly favoured') · dual ꜥꜣwy 'the two doors, the double door' (noun; written with the door-leaf twice)
glossary.wr: wr — great (adjective); a great one, a great amount (noun)
glossary.hꜣb: hꜣb — to be harmed, suffer loss (?) (verb; not otherwise known in this sense, and not hꜣb 'send'; reading and meaning uncertain; Budge: hab) · a second word of the same spelling: to send, send out (verb; Budge: habi, 'made to depart')
glossary.ḫnty: ḫnty — foremost, who is at the head of (nisba adjective; ḫnty imntt "Foremost of the West", a title of Osiris) · a second word of the same spelling: a pigment or colour (noun; reading doubtful)
glossary.ẖt: ẖt — belly, body; womb; (of gods and people) the person, the innermost self (noun)
glossary.mꜣt: mꜣt — pleasing, pleasant (?) (adjective-verb; reading and sense uncertain, written with the heart as classifier of feeling; Budge: mat, 'pleasant')
glossary.sḫm: sḫm — power, might; sacred image, cult statue (noun) · also the verb 'prevail, have power (over: m)' (sḫm m 'have power over') · also Sekhem, Letopolis, a city of Horus north of Memphis (place name; Budge: Seχem)
glossary.ntf: ntf — he (3rd person masculine singular independent pronoun; ntf N 'he is N', a sentence without a verb)
glossary.rq: rq — to oppose, be hostile (verb); opposition, hostility (noun)
glossary.ink: ink — I (1st person singular independent pronoun; ink N "I am N")
glossary.wḏ: wḏ — to command, decree, ordain (verb) · also wḏt 'command, decree' (noun f., from the verb) · also wḏ 'command, decree' (noun m.)
glossary.sš: sš — scribe (noun; the palette-and-pen sign) · a second word of the same spelling: to pass, go through (verb; doubtful here) · also to write, draw, paint (verb; written with the scribe's palette) · also the noun 'writing, document, record' (noun m.) · also to open (a door), spread open (verb; said of doors and bolts) · a further word of the same spelling: nest (noun m.; written with the nest of young birds; dual sšwy)
glossary.ḥtp: ḥtp — to be content, at peace, to rest (verb); peace; offering (noun; m ḥtp "in peace")
glossary.imntt: imntt — the West, the realm of the dead
glossary.nfr: nfr — beautiful, good, perfect (adjective; follows its noun; verb 'be good'); also beauty, goodness (noun m.)
glossary.st: st — place, seat, throne (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: it, them (3rd person dependent pronoun, object of a verb, written s-t) · also, with the hill-country sign, the desert hills, the necropolis (?) (noun; sense uncertain) · the dependent pronoun is also written with s alone
glossary.ssn: ssn — to breathe, smell (verb 3-lit.; written with the nose as classifier; Budge: sesen 'smell')
glossary.nfw: nfw — breath, wind (noun; written with the sail, which also writes ṯꜣw 'wind, breath')
glossary.wn: wn — to open (verb; wn n "open to") · also wn 'fault, failing, wrong' (noun)
glossary.nm: nm — who? (interrogative pronoun; later also written with ꜥ, nim) · m nm 'again, a second time' (?) (adverbial phrase; sense uncertain; Budge: em nem)
glossary.tr: tr — then, now, pray (enclitic particle that presses a question) · a second word of the same spelling: time, season (noun m.; dual trwy 'the two times', morning and evening)
glossary.tw: tw — you (2nd person masculine singular dependent pronoun; object of a verb, or subject after mk)
glossary.ntk: ntk — you (independent pronoun, 2nd person masculine singular; ntk N 'you are N', a sentence without a verb)
glossary.sbi: sbi — to go, pass, travel (verb; participle sby "one who passes")
glossary.ḫpr: ḫpr — to come into being, happen, become (verb)
glossary.wꜥ: wꜥ — one; (as a noun) one (of), someone
glossary.nty: nty — who, which, that (relative adjective); as a noun "he who"
glossary.mrty: mrty — Merty, a pair of goddesses (?) (god's name, dual; written with two eyes and the rearing cobra; the meaning of the name is not certain; Budge: Merti)
glossary.pw: pw — this, that (demonstrative, after its noun); 'it is' in nominal sentences (A pw 'it is A') · a second word of the same spelling: who? what? (interrogative pronoun; pw tr 'what then?')
glossary.rwi: rwi — to go away, depart (from: r) (verb; Budge: ruà, 'separate')
glossary.tp: tp — head, top; ḥry tp "who is upon" (noun) · also in the compound preposition ḥr-tp 'upon' · also the preposition tp 'upon' (tp tꜣ 'upon earth')
glossary.tkn: tkn — to approach, draw near (verb; tkn m "come near to")
glossary.msqt: msqt — the Meseqet, a place in the world below (place name; meaning of the name not clear; Budge: Mesqet)
glossary.sꜣq: sꜣq — robbery, theft (Budge reads the damaged sin here with a query) · to gather, collect, put together (verb; Budge: saqa)
glossary.bꜣ: bꜣ — ba, soul; the Ram, the ba-ram of Mendes (noun)
glossary.nšny: nšny — storm, raging (noun; from nšn 'rage'; Budge: neśeni)
glossary.šn: šn — to revile, curse(?) (verb; reading and sense uncertain, perhaps for šnṯ 'revile') · a second word of the same spelling: hair (noun; written with the cord šn and the lock of hair; Budge: śen)
glossary.wsr: wsr — power, strength (noun); to be strong, powerful (verb); strong (adjective) · a second word of the same spelling: oar (noun m.; plural wsrw, written with the wood classifier; Budge: useru)
glossary.srt: srt — goad, thorn (?) (noun f.; a pointed thing of wood, written with thorn and branch as classifiers; Budge: sert, 'goad')
glossary.mḏꜣbt: mḏꜣbt — meaning uncertain (?), a part of the boat (noun f.; written with the wood classifier; Budge: mat'abet, 'the hold')
glossary.smt: smt — not known (word of doubtful reading; Budge: semet, 'making straight for')
glossary.ꜥqꜣ: ꜥqꜣ — straight, exact (adjective; Budge: āqa, 'the middle')
glossary.ḥmw: ḥmw — steering-oar, rudder (noun m.; Budge: ḥemu)
glossary.mitt: mitt — likewise, the like, a like thing (adverb; noun f.; Budge: màtet)
glossary.stwt: stwt — rays, beams of light, esp. of the sun (noun f. plural; Budge: satetu) · a second word of the same spelling: meaning uncertain (?), written with a mummy-shaped classifier of images, perhaps from twt 'image' (noun)
glossary.qrs: qrs — to bury (verb) · qrst, burial (noun f.; the t is sometimes not written)
glossary.swn: swn — meaning uncertain (?), the name of some water, pool or lake (?) (noun; Budge: sun, 'the lake')
glossary.mhr: mhr — jug, milk-jug (?) (noun m.; written with a lidded pot as classifier; Budge: māḥerà)
glossary.irtt: irtt — milk (noun f.; written with the eye ir and the milk-jug in its net)
glossary.psy: psy — a kind of bread or loaf (?) (noun; reading doubtful, classified by the loaf; Budge: pasi, 'loaves')
glossary.dni: dni — to hold back, restrain, turn back (verb) · a second word of the same spelling: share, portion (?) (noun; Budge: ṭenà, 'portion')
glossary.inpw: inpw — Anubis, the jackal god of the cemetery and of embalming (god's name; Budge: Ànpu)
glossary.ꜥq: ꜥq — to enter, go in (verb; ꜥq r "enter into")
glossary.m-ḫt: m-ḫt — after, behind, in the following of (compound preposition: m 'in' + ḫt 'rear'; before a verb 'after he has …')
glossary.pri: pri — to go out, come forth (verb)
glossary.nht: nht — sycamore, sycamore-tree (noun f.; written with the tree and wood classifiers; Budge: nehet)
glossary.twy: twy — this, that (feminine demonstrative, after its noun)
glossary.nwt: nwt — Nut, the sky-goddess, mother of the sun and of Osiris (god's name; Budge: Nut) · a second word of the same spelling: bonds, wrappings (?) (noun f. plural; Budge: netu) · a third word (?): a weapon or tool (noun f.; doubtful; Budge: nut(?))
glossary.·t: ·t — you, your (2nd person feminine singular suffix pronoun; the bread-loaf sign)
glossary.sḫn: sḫn — to stir up, provoke · to embrace (verb; with the embracing arms as classifier; Budge: seχen)
glossary.ḥry-ib: ḥry-ib — middle, midst (noun; lit. "what is upon the heart"; m ḥry-ib "in the midst of") · also the inside, inner parts (of the body) · also who is in the midst of, who dwells in (nisba epithet after a noun or name; nṯr ꜥꜣ ḥry-ib ꜣbḏw 'the great god who dwells in Abydos')
glossary.wnw: wnw — Wenu, Hermopolis, city of Thoth in Middle Egypt, where the world was said to begin (place name; written with the hare wn and the town sign; Budge: Unnu)
glossary.sꜣw: sꜣw — Sais · a second word of the same spelling: to guard, keep watch (verb; written with the herdsman with his stick; Budge: sau) · also written with the sign sꜣ and the captive classifier, of keeping prisoners in custody (Budge: saiu)
glossary.ngg-wr: ngg-wr — Negeg-wer, 'the Great Cackler', a goose god of the beginning of things (god's name; from ngg 'cackle' and wr 'great'; Budge: Neḳeḳ ur)
glossary.rd: rd — foot, leg (noun; dual rd·fy "his two feet") · a second word of the same spelling: to grow (verb) · also thigh (?) (rtw, written with t for d; the sense is only a guess)
glossary.·s: ·s — she, her, it, its (3rd person feminine singular suffix pronoun; the folded cloth or the bolt)
